onnx_patterns#

This module documents the C++ optimization-pattern headers used by lib_onnx_patterns.

Core

namespace onnx_light

Alias that makes onnx-light headers compatible with code that references ONNX_LIGHT_NAMESPACE (the macro used in the standard onnx package).

Set to ONNX_LIGHT_NAMESPACE so both names resolve to the same namespace.

Symbol-visibility attribute for the public onnx-light C++ API.

Maps the upstream compatibility macro to onnx-light’s explicit proto ABI annotation. This keeps declarations from vendored ONNX headers visible when lib_onnx_proto uses hidden visibility by default.

Namespace alias so that ONNX C++ code (and consumers such as onnxruntime) that refers to the literal onnx namespace — rather than the ONNX_NAMESPACE macro — resolves to the onnx-light namespace. The standard onnx package lives in namespace onnx; onnx-light uses onnx_light (via ONNX_LIGHT_NAMESPACE), so this alias keeps onnx-light a true drop-in. It is only introduced when the onnx-light namespace differs from onnx.

namespace onnx_patterns#

Functions

void RegisterPatterns()#

Registers every built-in ONNX graph-rewriting pattern.

Registration is idempotent. Call this function before :cpp:func:core::builder::CreateRegisteredPatterns when the standard ONNX pattern set is required.

std::unique_ptr<core::builder::PatternOptimization> CreatePattern(const std::string &name, std::optional<int> priority = std::nullopt)#

Creates one standard ONNX pattern by registered name.

Registration is ensured before lookup. When priority is specified, it overrides the pattern default.

namespace onnx_patterns
class SameChildrenFromInputPattern : public onnx_light::onnx_patterns::SameChildrenPattern#
#include <common_pattern.h>

Merges identical nodes that consume the same graph input.

Before:
                        +---------+
  graph_input, c -----> | Op      | -----> a
                        +---------+

                        +---------+
  graph_input, c -----> | Op      | -----> b
                        +---------+

After:
                        +---------+
  graph_input, c -----> | Op      | -----> a
                        +---------+
                              |
                              v
                       +----------+
                       | Identity | -----> b
                       +----------+

It uses the same replacement as SameChildrenPattern, retaining one node and preserving every removed sibling output with an Identity.

Public Functions

inline explicit SameChildrenFromInputPattern(int priority = 0)#
virtual core::builder::MatchResult Match(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const NodeProto &candidate) const override#

Returns the match rooted at candidate. A null pattern means no match.

class SameChildrenPattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <common_pattern.h>

Merges pairs of identical sibling nodes, and any identical descendant chains.

Before:
                   +----+                       +------+
           +-----> | Op | ---> a ------------> | Next | ---> p
           |       +----+                       +------+
           |
  x, c ----+
           |
           |       +----+                       +------+
           +-----> | Op | ---> b ------------> | Next | ---> q
                   +----+                       +------+

After:
            +----+             +------+
  x, c ---> | Op | ---> a ---> | Next | ---> p
            +----+      |      +------+      |
                        |                    |
                        v                    v
                   +----------+         +----------+
                   | Identity | ---> b  | Identity | ---> q
                   +----------+         +----------+

One copy of every equivalent node is retained. Identity nodes preserve all output names from the removed copy, including outputs used by later nodes.

Subclassed by onnx_light::onnx_patterns::SameChildrenFromInputPattern

Public Functions

inline explicit SameChildrenPattern(int priority = 0)#
virtual core::builder::MatchResult Match(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const NodeProto &candidate) const override#

Returns the match rooted at candidate. A null pattern means no match.

virtual utils::RepeatedProtoField<NodeProto> Apply(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const std::vector<const NodeProto*> &nodes) const override#

Builds the replacement nodes for one match.

Protected Functions

inline SameChildrenPattern(int priority, std::string name)#
core::builder::MatchResult MatchWithNodes(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const NodeProto &candidate, const std::vector<const NodeProto*> &next_nodes) const#

static bool SameNode(const NodeProto &first, const NodeProto &second)#

class ShapeBasedIdentityPattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <common_pattern.h>

Replaces a shape-preserving Slice by an Identity.

Before:
  x, starts, ends, axes, steps=1
               |
               v
        +---------+
        | Slice   |
        +---------+
               |
               v
               y

After:
         +----------+
  x ---> | Identity | ---> y
         +----------+

The rewrite requires equal inferred input and output shapes. When the optional steps input is present, it must be a materialized all-one constant.

Public Functions

inline explicit ShapeBasedIdentityPattern(int priority = 0)#
virtual std::set<std::string> FastOpType() const override#

Returns the invariant operator types from which this pattern can start. The optimization driver caches this value once per optimization.

virtual core::builder::MatchResult Match(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const NodeProto &candidate) const override#

Returns the match rooted at candidate. A null pattern means no match.

virtual utils::RepeatedProtoField<NodeProto> Apply(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const std::vector<const NodeProto*> &nodes) const override#

Builds the replacement nodes for one match.

class ShapeBasedSameChildrenPattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <common_pattern.h>

Merges Expand or Reshape siblings whose inferred output shapes are equal.

Before:
                   +---------+
  x, shape1 -----> | Reshape | -----> a
                   +---------+

                   +---------+
  x, shape2 -----> | Reshape | -----> b
                   +---------+

After:
                   +---------+
  x, shape1 -----> | Reshape | -----> a
                   +---------+
                         |
                         v
                  +----------+
                  | Identity | -----> b
                  +----------+

The inferred shapes of a and b must be equal, although the shape inputs may differ. The first operation is retained and each other sibling is replaced by an Identity that retains its original output name.

Public Functions

inline explicit ShapeBasedSameChildrenPattern(int priority = 0)#
virtual std::set<std::string> FastOpType() const override#

Returns the invariant operator types from which this pattern can start. The optimization driver caches this value once per optimization.

virtual core::builder::MatchResult Match(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const NodeProto &candidate) const override#

Returns the match rooted at candidate. A null pattern means no match.

virtual utils::RepeatedProtoField<NodeProto> Apply(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const std::vector<const NodeProto*> &nodes) const override#

Builds the replacement nodes for one match.

class SwapUnaryPattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <common_pattern.h>

Moves a rank-preserving layout operation after a compatible following operation.

Before:
  x, perm/shape
        |
        v
  +-------------------+
  | Transpose/Reshape |
  +-------------------+
        |
        v
  +---------+
  | Unary   | <--- extra inputs
  +---------+
        |
        v
        y

After:
         +---------+
  x ---> | Unary   | <--- extra inputs
         +---------+
              |
              v
       +-------------------+
       | Transpose/Reshape | <--- perm/shape
       +-------------------+
              |
              v
              y

The layout node is a Transpose or Reshape. The following node is unary-like, or is Add, Sub, Mul, or Div with a shape-[1] second input; its extra inputs and the final output name are retained.

Public Functions

inline explicit SwapUnaryPattern(int priority = 0)#
virtual std::set<std::string> FastOpType() const override#

Returns the invariant operator types from which this pattern can start. The optimization driver caches this value once per optimization.

virtual core::builder::MatchResult Match(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const NodeProto &candidate) const override#

Returns the match rooted at candidate. A null pattern means no match.

virtual utils::RepeatedProtoField<NodeProto> Apply(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const std::vector<const NodeProto*> &nodes) const override#

Builds the replacement nodes for one match.

namespace onnx_patterns
class MulMulMulScalarPattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <mul_pattern.h>

Combines the scalar constants from three nested Mul or Div nodes.

Before:
             +---------+
  a, c1 ---> | LeftOp  | ---> l
             +---------+

             +---------+
  b, c2 ---> | RightOp | ---> r
             +---------+

           +---------+
  l, r --> | OuterOp | ---> y
           +---------+

After:
            +---------+
  a, b ---> | OuterOp | ---> t
            +---------+

                         +---------+
  t, combined scalar --> | Mul/Div | ---> y
                         +---------+

c1 and c2 are scalar or one-element constants. The replacement retains the outer output and combines or reciprocates the constants as required by the inner Mul/Div operators; two inner Div nodes produce the final Div, while all other combinations produce the final Mul.

Public Functions

inline explicit MulMulMulScalarPattern(int priority = 0)#
virtual std::set<std::string> FastOpType() const override#

Returns the invariant operator types from which this pattern can start. The optimization driver caches this value once per optimization.

virtual core::builder::MatchResult Match(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const NodeProto &candidate) const override#

Returns the match rooted at candidate. A null pattern means no match.

virtual utils::RepeatedProtoField<NodeProto> Apply(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const std::vector<const NodeProto*> &nodes) const override#

Builds the replacement nodes for one match.

class SwitchOrderBinaryPattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <mul_pattern.h>

Reassociates nested Add or Mul nodes to reduce broadcasting rank.

Before:
            +---------+
  b, c ---> | Add/Mul | ---> t
            +---------+
                 |
                 v
           +---------+
           | Add/Mul | <--- a
           +---------+
                 |
                 v
                 y

After:
            +---------+
  b, a ---> | Add/Mul | ---> t2
            +---------+
                 |
                 v
           +---------+
           | Add/Mul | <--- c
           +---------+
                 |
                 v
                 y

Alternative matched forms may group (c, a), or place the inner node on the
right input of the outer node.

The symmetric right-nested form is also handled, and the alternative Op(c, a) grouping may be selected. The inner output must be unshared; the outer output name is retained.

Public Functions

inline explicit SwitchOrderBinaryPattern(int priority = 0)#
virtual std::set<std::string> FastOpType() const override#

Returns the invariant operator types from which this pattern can start. The optimization driver caches this value once per optimization.

virtual core::builder::MatchResult Match(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const NodeProto &candidate) const override#

Returns the match rooted at candidate. A null pattern means no match.

virtual utils::RepeatedProtoField<NodeProto> Apply(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const std::vector<const NodeProto*> &nodes) const override#

Builds the replacement nodes for one match.

namespace onnx_patterns
class SwapRangeAddScalarPattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <range_pattern.h>

Moves a shape-[1] second Add input from after Range into its start and limit inputs.

Before:
  start, limit, delta
          |
          v
      +-------+
      | Range | ---> r
      +-------+
          |
          v
       +-----+
       | Add | <--- offset
       +-----+
          |
          v
          y

After:
                               +-----+
  start ----------------------> | Add | ---> start2 ----------------+
                               +-----+                              |
                                  ^                                 |
                                  |                                 |
              +---------+         |                                 |
  offset ---> | Squeeze | ---> s -+                                 |
              +---------+         |                                 |
                                  v                                 |
                               +-----+                              |
  limit ----------------------> | Add | ---> limit2 ----------------+--+
                               +-----+                                 |
                                                                       v
                                                                   +-------+
  delta ---------------------------------------------------------> | Range | ---> y
                                                                   +-------+

After (start is constant zero):
              +---------+
  offset ---> | Squeeze | ---> s -----------------------------------+
              +---------+
                                 |                                  |
                                 v                                  |
                              +-----+                               |
  limit ---------------------> | Add | ---> limit2 -----------------+--+
                              +-----+                                  |
                                                                        v
                                                                    +-------+
  delta ----------------------------------------------------------> | Range | ---> y
                                                                    +-------+

When start is the constant zero, start2 is s and its Add is omitted. The Range and Add are replaced while the Add output y, the offset, and any Range step input are retained.

Public Functions

inline explicit SwapRangeAddScalarPattern(int priority = 0)#
virtual std::set<std::string> FastOpType() const override#

Returns the invariant operator types from which this pattern can start. The optimization driver caches this value once per optimization.

virtual core::builder::MatchResult Match(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const NodeProto &candidate) const override#

Returns the match rooted at candidate. A null pattern means no match.

virtual utils::RepeatedProtoField<NodeProto> Apply(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const std::vector<const NodeProto*> &nodes) const override#

Builds the replacement nodes for one match.

Namespace alias so that ONNX C++ code (and consumers such as onnxruntime) that refers to the literal onnx namespace — rather than the ONNX_NAMESPACE macro — resolves to the onnx-light namespace. The standard onnx package lives in namespace onnx; onnx-light uses onnx_light (via ONNX_LIGHT_NAMESPACE), so this alias keeps onnx-light a true drop-in. It is only introduced when the onnx-light namespace differs from onnx.

class ReduceArgTopKPattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <reduce_pattern.h>

Fuses matching ReduceMin/ReduceMax and ArgMin/ArgMax nodes into TopK with K=1.

Before:
                   +---------------+
           +-----> | ReduceMax/Min | ---> values
           |       +---------------+
           |
  x -------+
           |
           |       +------------+
           +-----> | ArgMax/Min | ---> indices
                   +------------+

After:
                +------+
  x, K=[1] ---> | TopK |
                +------+
                   |
             +-----+-----+
             |           |
             v           v
          values      indices

After (keepdims=0):
                +------+
  x, K=[1] ---> | TopK |
                +------+
                   |
             +-----+-----+
             |           |
             v           v
     temporary values  temporary indices
             |           |
             v           v
         +---------+  +---------+
  axes -> | Squeeze |  | Squeeze | <- axes
         +---------+  +---------+
             |           |
             v           v
          values      indices

The Min variant sets largest=0. When keepdims=0, TopK produces temporary singleton-axis outputs and two Squeeze nodes restore the original values and indices output names.

class ReduceSumNormalizePattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <reduce_pattern.h>

Moves a Cast-ReduceSum-Mul-Sub-Cast normalization chain to the result type.

Before:
         +------+
  x ---> | Cast | ---> xc
         +------+
            |
            v
      +-----------+
      | ReduceSum | <--- axes
      +-----------+
            |
            v
         +-----+
         | Mul | <--- scale
         +-----+
            |
            v
         +-----+
         | Sub | <--- xc (or axes)
         +-----+
            |
            v
         +------+
         | Cast | ---> y
         +------+

After:
         +-----------+
  x ---> | ReduceSum | <--- axes
         +-----------+
              |
              v
           +-----+      +------+
           | Mul | <--- | Cast | <--- scale
           +-----+      +------+
              |
              v
           +-----+
           | Sub | <--- x
           +-----+
              |
              v
              y

The reversed Sub operand order is retained. The five matched nodes become ReduceSum, Cast, Mul, and Sub nodes in T while preserving axes, scale, ReduceSum attributes, and the final output y. The matcher also accepts axes instead of xc as the reused Sub input; Apply replaces that reused input with x in either case.

class Sub1MulPattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <sub_pattern.h>

Rewrites multiplication by 1 - x into a product followed by subtraction.

Before:
              +-----+
  one, x ---> | Sub | ---> d
              +-----+
                 |
                 v
              +-----+
              | Mul | <--- z
              +-----+
                 |
                 v
                 y

After:
            +-----+
  x, z ---> | Mul | ---> p
            +-----+
               |
               v
            +-----+
  z ------> | Sub | ---> y
            +-----+

The symmetric Mul input order is supported. one may come from an all-one ConstantOfShape when output-shape preservation is proven; z and the final output y are retained.

class AttentionGQAPattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <attention_pattern.h>

Converts cached grouped-query attention into ONNX Attention cache inputs and outputs.

Before:
  ONNX decomposition, Reshape form:

    Q  past K     K                            past V     V                     mask
    |     |       |                               |       |                       |
    |     v       v                               v       v                       |
    | +---------------+                       +---------------+                   |
    | |    Concat     |                       |    Concat     |                   |
    | +---------------+                       +---------------+                   |
    |         |    axes 2                             |    axes 2                 |
    |         |       |                               |       |                   |
    |         v       v                               v       v                   |
    |     +---------------+                       +---------------+               |
    |     |   Unsqueeze   |                       |   Unsqueeze   |               |
    |     +---------------+                       +---------------+               |
    |             |   expand shape                        |   expand shape        |
    |             |       |                               |       |               |
    |             v       v                               v       v               |
    |         +---------------+                       +---------------+           |
    |         |    Expand     |                       |    Expand     |           |
    |         +---------------+                       +---------------+           |
    |                 |   gqa shape                           |   gqa shape       |
    |                 |       |                               |       |           |
    |                 v       v                               v       v           |
    |             +---------------+                       +---------------+       |
    |             |    Reshape    |                       |    Reshape    |       |
    |             +---------------+                       +---------------+       |
    |                     |                                       |               |
    v                     v                                       v               v
  +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
  |                                     Attention                                     |
  +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
                                            |
                                            v
                                            Y

  ONNX decomposition, Squeeze form:

    Q  past K     K                            past V     V                     mask
    |     |       |                               |       |                       |
    |     v       v                               v       v                       |
    | +---------------+                       +---------------+                   |
    | |    Concat     |                       |    Concat     |                   |
    | +---------------+                       +---------------+                   |
    |         |    axes 2                             |    axes 2                 |
    |         |       |                               |       |                   |
    |         v       v                               v       v                   |
    |     +---------------+                       +---------------+               |
    |     |   Unsqueeze   |                       |   Unsqueeze   |               |
    |     +---------------+                       +---------------+               |
    |             |   expand shape                        |   expand shape        |
    |             |       |                               |       |               |
    |             v       v                               v       v               |
    |         +---------------+                       +---------------+           |
    |         |    Expand     |                       |    Expand     |           |
    |         +---------------+                       +---------------+           |
    |                 |   squeeze axes                        |   squeeze axes    |
    |                 |       |                               |       |           |
    |                 v       v                               v       v           |
    |             +---------------+                       +---------------+       |
    |             |    Squeeze    |                       |    Squeeze    |       |
    |             +---------------+                       +---------------+       |
    |                     |                                       |               |
    v                     v                                       v               v
  +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
  |                                     Attention                                     |
  +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
                                            |
                                            v
                                            Y

  Local-function form:

    Q  past K     K          past V     V       mask    scale sqrt    expand shape  gqa shape
    |     |       |             |       |         |         |             |             |
    |     v       v             v       v         |         |             |             |
    | +---------------+     +---------------+     |         |             |             |
    | |    Concat     |     |    Concat     |     |         |             |             |
    | +---------------+     +---------------+     |         |             |             |
    |         |                     |             |         |             |             |
    v         v                     v             v         v             v             v
  +-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
  |                              intermediate::LocalAttentionGQA                              |
  +-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
                                                |
                                                v
                                                Y

After:
  Direct mask:

      Q         K         V       mask       past K        past V
      |         |         |         |           |             |
      v         v         v         v           v             v
  +---------------------------------------------------------------------+
  |                              Attention                              |
  +---------------------------------------------------------------------+
            |                   |                     |
            v                   v                     v
            Y               present K             present V

  Switched local mask:

                                  mask
                                    |
                                    v
                                +-------+
                                |  Not  |
                                +-------+
                                    |
      Q         K         V         |        past K        past V
      |         |         |         |           |             |
      v         v         v         v           v             v
  +---------------------------------------------------------------------+
  |                              Attention                              |
  +---------------------------------------------------------------------+
            |                   |                     |
            v                   v                     v
            Y               present K             present V

The caches and current tensors must be compatible rank-four values, and both cache Concat nodes use normalized axis 2. Opset 23 is required. The two cache Concat results become the present-cache outputs of the new Attention node. The Not box appears only for switched local masks, which must be bool. The ONNX form copies the scale and is_causal attributes, while the local scale_sqrt input is squared into the Attention scale attribute.

class FunctionAttentionGQAPattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <attention_pattern.h>

Moves matching GQA repeat-interleave branches into a LocalAttention function.

Before:
  Reshape form:

    Q         K    axes 2                     V    axes 2               mask      scale
    |         |       |                       |       |                   |         |
    |         v       v                       v       v                   |         |
    |     +---------------+               +---------------+               |         |
    |     |   Unsqueeze   |               |   Unsqueeze   |               |         |
    |     +---------------+               +---------------+               |         |
    |             |   expand shape                |   expand shape        |         |
    |             |       |                       |       |               |         |
    |             v       v                       v       v               |         |
    |         +---------------+               +---------------+           |         |
    |         |    Expand     |               |    Expand     |           |         |
    |         +---------------+               +---------------+           |         |
    |                 |   gqa shape                   |   gqa shape       |         |
    |                 |       |                       |       |           |         |
    |                 v       v                       v       v           |         |
    |             +---------------+               +---------------+       |         |
    |             |    Reshape    |               |    Reshape    |       |         |
    |             +---------------+               +---------------+       |         |
    |                     |                               |               |         |
    v                     v                               v               v         v
  +-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
  |                            intermediate::LocalAttention                             |
  +-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
                                             |
                                             v
                                             Y

  Squeeze form:

    Q         K    axes 2                     V    axes 2               mask      scale
    |         |       |                       |       |                   |         |
    |         v       v                       v       v                   |         |
    |     +---------------+               +---------------+               |         |
    |     |   Unsqueeze   |               |   Unsqueeze   |               |         |
    |     +---------------+               +---------------+               |         |
    |             |   expand shape                |   expand shape        |         |
    |             |       |                       |       |               |         |
    |             v       v                       v       v               |         |
    |         +---------------+               +---------------+           |         |
    |         |    Expand     |               |    Expand     |           |         |
    |         +---------------+               +---------------+           |         |
    |                 |   squeeze axes                |   squeeze axes    |         |
    |                 |       |                       |       |           |         |
    |                 v       v                       v       v           |         |
    |             +---------------+               +---------------+       |         |
    |             |    Squeeze    |               |    Squeeze    |       |         |
    |             +---------------+               +---------------+       |         |
    |                     |                               |               |         |
    v                     v                               v               v         v
  +-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
  |                            intermediate::LocalAttention                             |
  +-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
                                             |
                                             v
                                             Y

After:

      Q         K         V       mask      scale     expand shape  gqa shape
      |         |         |         |         |           |             |
      v         v         v         v         v           v             v
  +---------------------------------------------------------------------------+
  |                      intermediate::LocalAttentionGQA                      |
  +---------------------------------------------------------------------------+
                                        |
                                        v
                                        Y

Key and value branches must use identical constant shapes, rank-five Expand targets with singleton non-repeat dimensions, and the same final operation. The Reshape form ends on a rank-four shape while the Squeeze form ends on a single axis, so the last call input is a shape or an axis accordingly. Inputs must be floating and every removed repeat intermediate unshared. The concrete local-function name records Reshape versus Squeeze and retains the original attention suffix.

              |                       intermediate::LocalAttention                        |
              +---------------------------------------------------------------------------+
                                                    |
                                                    v
                                                    Y

The four score paths and the three masking forms combine freely; each drawing shows one legal pairing. The additive form needs

Where(mask, zero, minus

infinity)

, the direct form places negative infinity on the third Where input, and the switched form places it on the second one. Softmax uses axis -1 and opset 18 or newer is required. The rank-four key Transpose uses permutation 0, 1, 3, 2 and the rank-three one 0, 2, 3, 1, while FusedMatMul must set transA=0, transB=1, and alpha=1. Rank-three inputs need matching Reshape targets, and Apply rebuilds both branches with permutation 0, 2, 1, 3. Query and key scales must be equal floating scalars, the GQA key and value repeat shapes must match, and every removed result is unshared. The emitted function name encodes GQA, the switched mask, the missing transpose, and the element type; GQA additionally appends the expand and repeat shapes to the call.

Canonicalization

namespace onnx_light

Alias that makes onnx-light headers compatible with code that references ONNX_LIGHT_NAMESPACE (the macro used in the standard onnx package).

Set to ONNX_LIGHT_NAMESPACE so both names resolve to the same namespace.

Symbol-visibility attribute for the public onnx-light C++ API.

Maps the upstream compatibility macro to onnx-light’s explicit proto ABI annotation. This keeps declarations from vendored ONNX headers visible when lib_onnx_proto uses hidden visibility by default.

Namespace alias so that ONNX C++ code (and consumers such as onnxruntime) that refers to the literal onnx namespace — rather than the ONNX_NAMESPACE macro — resolves to the onnx-light namespace. The standard onnx package lives in namespace onnx; onnx-light uses onnx_light (via ONNX_LIGHT_NAMESPACE), so this alias keeps onnx-light a true drop-in. It is only introduced when the onnx-light namespace differs from onnx.

class CastCastPattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <cast_pattern.h>

Canonicalizes consecutive Cast nodes when a single conversion is equivalent.

Before:
           +-----------+               +-----------+
  x:A ---> | Cast to B | ---> m:B ---> | Cast to C | ---> y:C
           +-----------+               +-----------+

After:
           +------------+
  x:A ---> | Cast to C* | ---> y:C
           +------------+

After (no conversion is needed):
           +----------+
  x:A ---> | Identity | ---> y:C
           +----------+

After (the intermediate m:B is shared):
           +-----------+
  x:A ---> | Cast to B | ---> m:B ---> other consumer
           +-----------+

           +------------+
  x:A ---> | Cast to C* | ---> y:C
           +------------+

C* denotes the single safe replacement type selected from the input, intermediate, and final types. If m has another consumer, the first Cast is retained for that consumer while y is still produced directly from x.

class CastOpCastPattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <cast_pattern.h>

Moves an operation from a temporary floating-point type to its result type.

Before:
           +-----------+
  y:R ---> | Cast to C | ---> yc:C
           +-----------+

                +----+
  x:C, yc:C --> | Op | ---> t:C
                +----+
                  |
                  v
             +-----------+
             | Cast to R | ---> z:R
             +-----------+

After:
           +-----------+
  x:C ---> | Cast to R | ---> xr:R
           +-----------+

               +----+
  xr:R, y:R -> | Op | ---> z:R
               +----+

After (the original Op output t:C is shared):
           +-----------+
  z:R ---> | Cast to C | ---> t:C
           +-----------+

The unary form uses the same rewrite with one input.

Inputs already produced in R lose their Cast; other inputs gain one. The unary case follows the same transformation with a single input. If the original Op:C output is retained elsewhere, a Cast from z:R back to that output in C is also emitted.

Creates the pattern with the given optimization priority.

Returns the supported unary and binary operator types.

virtual core::builder::MatchResult Match(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const NodeProto &candidate) const override#

Finds an operation between compatible input and output Cast nodes.

virtual utils::RepeatedProtoField<NodeProto> Apply(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const std::vector<const NodeProto*> &nodes) const override#

Rebuilds the operation in the output type and removes the surrounding Cast nodes.

namespace onnx_light

Alias that makes onnx-light headers compatible with code that references ONNX_LIGHT_NAMESPACE (the macro used in the standard onnx package).

Set to ONNX_LIGHT_NAMESPACE so both names resolve to the same namespace.

Symbol-visibility attribute for the public onnx-light C++ API.

Maps the upstream compatibility macro to onnx-light’s explicit proto ABI annotation. This keeps declarations from vendored ONNX headers visible when lib_onnx_proto uses hidden visibility by default.

Namespace alias so that ONNX C++ code (and consumers such as onnxruntime) that refers to the literal onnx namespace — rather than the ONNX_NAMESPACE macro — resolves to the onnx-light namespace. The standard onnx package lives in namespace onnx; onnx-light uses onnx_light (via ONNX_LIGHT_NAMESPACE), so this alias keeps onnx-light a true drop-in. It is only introduced when the onnx-light namespace differs from onnx.

namespace onnx_patterns
class ClipClipPattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <clip_pattern.h>

Merges two consecutive Clip nodes when one defines the minimum and the other the maximum.

Before:
              +------+
  x, min ---> | Clip | ---> t
              +------+
                 |
                 v
              +------+
              | Clip | <--- max
              +------+
                 |
                 v
                 y

After:
                   +------+
  x, min, max ---> | Clip | ---> y
                   +------+

The rewrite requires exactly one of the two Clip nodes to supply the minimum bound and exactly one to supply the maximum bound, so the merged Clip carries both bounds and retains the second Clip output. The first Clip output must not have another consumer.

Replaces the matched Clip pair with a single Clip carrying both bounds.

class PadConvPattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <conv_pattern.h>

Fuses a Pad node followed by a Conv node into a single Conv node whose pads attribute absorbs the spatial padding.

Before:
                        +-----+
  X, pads, value=0 ---> | Pad | ---> p
                        +-----+
                           |
                           v
                    +------+
                    | Conv | <--- W, B
                    +------+
                           |
                           v
                           Y

After:
               +--------------------+
  X, W, B ---> | Conv with new pads | ---> Y
               +--------------------+

class IdentityPattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <identity_pattern.h>

Replaces no-op operations by an Identity node.

The pattern recognises redundant arithmetic and layout operations such as Add(x, 0), Mul(x, 1), Sub(x, 0), Div(x, 1), Or(x, false), And(x, true), Transpose(x, perm=[0, 1, 2, ...]), Reshape(x, [0, 0, ...]), a full-range Slice, an Expand with an all-one target shape of the input rank, and a half-precision inference BatchNormalization with scale/bias/mean/variance constants 1/0/0/1.

Before:
              +-----+
  x, zero --> | Add | ---> y
              +-----+

After:
         +----------+
  x ---> | Identity | ---> y
         +----------+

The no-op node is replaced while its selected data input and first output name are retained; neutral constants no longer feed that output.

class ConcatEmptyPattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <concat_pattern.h>

Removes Concat inputs that are empty along the concatenation axis.

An input is dropped when its inferred size along axis is exactly zero, so it contributes nothing to the output. When a single input remains the Concat becomes an Identity; otherwise a narrower Concat is emitted with the same axis.

Before:
             +--------------+
  x, e, z -> | Concat axis0 | ---> y
             +--------------+

After:
          +--------------+
  x, z -> | Concat axis0 | ---> y
          +--------------+

After (one non-empty input remains):
         +----------+
  x ---> | Identity | ---> y
         +----------+

The inferred size of e along axis 0 is zero.

Public Functions

inline explicit ConcatEmptyPattern(int priority = 0)#

Creates the pattern with the given optimization priority.

virtual std::set<std::string> FastOpType() const override#

Returns Concat as the only possible root operator.

virtual core::builder::MatchResult Match(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const NodeProto &candidate) const override#

Finds a Concat with at least one empty input along its axis.

virtual utils::RepeatedProtoField<NodeProto> Apply(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const std::vector<const NodeProto*> &nodes) const override#

Rebuilds the Concat (or an Identity) without the empty inputs.

class ConcatGatherPattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <concat_pattern.h>

Simplifies Gather(Concat(...), cst_index) when the index is a constant single-element int64 tensor and every Concat input is a 1-D tensor of a statically known size.

The pattern locates which Concat input holds the addressed element and replaces the Gather with an Identity (single-element input), a narrower Shape (input produced by a ranged Shape), or a Gather with a locally adjusted index.

Before:
               +--------------+
  a, b, c ---> | Concat axis0 | ---> t
               +--------------+
                      |
                      v
                 +--------------+
                 | Gather axis0 | <--- index=[3]
                 +--------------+
                      |
                      v
                      y

After:
                    +--------------+
  b, index=[1] ---> | Gather axis0 | ---> y
                    +--------------+

After (the selected input has one element):
         +----------+
  b ---> | Identity | ---> y
         +----------+

After (the selected input is produced by Shape):
         +-------------------------+
  x ---> | Shape adjusted interval | ---> y
         +-------------------------+

If t has another consumer, the original Concat is retained for that consumer.

Public Functions

inline explicit ConcatGatherPattern(int priority = 0)#

Creates the pattern with the given optimization priority.

virtual std::set<std::string> FastOpType() const override#

Returns Gather as the only possible root operator.

virtual core::builder::MatchResult Match(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const NodeProto &candidate) const override#

Finds a constant-index Gather over a fully-shaped Concat.

virtual utils::RepeatedProtoField<NodeProto> Apply(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const std::vector<const NodeProto*> &nodes) const override#

Rewrites the Gather against the located Concat input.

class ConcatTwiceUnaryPattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <concat_pattern.h>

Pushes a shape-preserving unary operator through a Concat(x, x) so that Unary(Concat(x, x)) becomes Concat(Unary(x), Unary(x)), exposing the shared Unary(x) for common-subexpression elimination.

The rewrite requires opset >= 18, a two-input Concat whose inputs are the same value, and a consumer that is a shape-preserving unary op (or a broadcasting Mul / Add / Div / Sub / Unsqueeze with a constant scalar second input).

Before:
          +--------+
  x, x -> | Concat | ---> t
          +--------+

         +-------+
  t ---> | Unary | ---> y
         +-------+

After:
         +-------+
  x ---> | Unary | ---> u
         +-------+

          +--------+
  u, u -> | Concat | ---> y
          +--------+

If t has another consumer, Concat(x, x) is retained for it.

Public Functions

inline explicit ConcatTwiceUnaryPattern(int priority = 0)#

Creates the pattern with the given optimization priority.

Returns Concat as the only possible root operator.

virtual core::builder::MatchResult Match(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const NodeProto &candidate) const override#

Finds a Concat(x, x) consumed by a shape-preserving unary op.

virtual utils::RepeatedProtoField<NodeProto> Apply(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const std::vector<const NodeProto*> &nodes) const override#

Moves the unary op ahead of the Concat.

                     +--------------+
                          |
                          v

After:
  x, [7,4]
      |
      v
  +--------------+
  | Gather axis0 | ---> y
  +--------------+

namespace onnx_patterns
class SequenceConstructAtPattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <sequence_pattern.h>

Replaces SequenceConstruct(x0, x1, ...) followed by the matching SequenceAt(seq, 0), SequenceAt(seq, 1), … with one Identity per SequenceAt, forwarding the original tensor directly.

The rewrite requires every consumer of the sequence to be a SequenceAt with a constant scalar index, and the indices to cover 0 .. n-1 exactly once, so the sequence value becomes dead and is removed.

Before:
              +-------------------+
  x0, x1 ---> | SequenceConstruct | ---> s
              +-------------------+
                   |         |
                   v         v
          +------------+   +------------+
          | SequenceAt |   | SequenceAt |
          +------------+   +------------+
               | index=0        | index=1
               v                v
               y0               y1

After:
          +----------+
  x0 ---> | Identity | ---> y0
          +----------+

          +----------+
  x1 ---> | Identity | ---> y1
          +----------+

Public Functions

inline explicit SequenceConstructAtPattern(int priority = 0)#

Creates the pattern with the given optimization priority.

virtual std::set<std::string> FastOpType() const override#

Returns SequenceConstruct as the only possible root operator.

virtual core::builder::MatchResult Match(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const NodeProto &candidate) const override#

Finds a SequenceConstruct fully consumed by constant SequenceAt.

virtual utils::RepeatedProtoField<NodeProto> Apply(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const std::vector<const NodeProto*> &nodes) const override#

Replaces each SequenceAt with an Identity on the built tensor.

class SplitToSequenceSequenceAtPattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <sequence_pattern.h>

Replaces SplitToSequence(x, [split], axis=a) followed by the matching SequenceAt(seq, 0), SequenceAt(seq, 1), … with a single Split.

When keepdims=0, the replacement inserts a Squeeze on the split axis after every Split output to reproduce the corresponding SequenceAt result.

The indices of the SequenceAt consumers must be constant scalars that cover 0 .. n-1 exactly once.

Before:
         +-----------------+
  x ---> | SplitToSequence | ---> s
         +-----------------+
              |       |
              v       v
       +------------+ +------------+
       | SequenceAt | | SequenceAt |
       +------------+ +------------+
          | index=0     | index=1
          v             v
          y0            y1

After (keepdims=0):
         +-------+
  x ---> | Split | ---> t0, t1
         +-------+

                    +---------+
  t0, axes=[1] ---> | Squeeze | ---> y0
                    +---------+
                    +---------+
  t1, axes=[1] ---> | Squeeze | ---> y1
                    +---------+

After (keepdims=1):
         +-------+
  x ---> | Split | ---> y0, y1
         +-------+

With keepdims=1, the Split writes the SequenceAt outputs directly; an explicit split input is forwarded unchanged.

Public Functions

inline explicit SplitToSequenceSequenceAtPattern(int priority = 0)#

Creates the pattern with the given optimization priority.

virtual std::set<std::string> FastOpType() const override#

Returns SplitToSequence as the only possible root operator.

virtual core::builder::MatchResult Match(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const NodeProto &candidate) const override#

Finds a SplitToSequence fully consumed by constant SequenceAt.

virtual utils::RepeatedProtoField<NodeProto> Apply(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const std::vector<const NodeProto*> &nodes) const override#

Replaces the sequence with a Split (and Squeeze when needed).

namespace onnx_patterns
class GatherShapePattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <shape_pattern.h>

Simplifies Gather(Shape(X), indices) into Shape(X, start, end) when indices is a constant int64 scalar or a contiguous ascending 1-D range.

The start / end attributes possibly carried by the original Shape node are folded into the new bounds. A scalar index yields a Shape followed by a Squeeze of the leading axis to recover the 0-D result.

Before:
         +---------------------+
  x ---> | Shape start=1 end=5 | ---> s
         +---------------------+
                    |
                    v
             +--------------+
             | Gather axis0 | <--- indices=[1,2]
             +--------------+
                    |
                    v
                    y

After:
         +---------------------+
  x ---> | Shape start=2 end=4 | ---> y
         +---------------------+

After (scalar index):
         +---------------------+
  x ---> | Shape start=2 end=3 | ---> s
         +---------------------+
                   |
                   v
              +---------+
              | Squeeze | <--- axes=[0]
              +---------+
                   |
                   v
                   y

For scalar index 1, the result is Squeeze(Shape(x,start=2,end=3),axes=[0]). If s has another consumer, the original Shape is retained.

Public Functions

inline explicit GatherShapePattern(int priority = 0)#

Creates the pattern with the given optimization priority.

virtual std::set<std::string> FastOpType() const override#

Returns Gather as the only possible root operator.

virtual core::builder::MatchResult Match(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const NodeProto &candidate) const override#

Finds a contiguous constant-index Gather over a Shape.

virtual utils::RepeatedProtoField<NodeProto> Apply(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const std::vector<const NodeProto*> &nodes) const override#

Rewrites the pair into a bounded Shape (plus Squeeze if scalar).

class ShapeTransposePattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <shape_pattern.h>

Replaces Shape(Transpose(X, perm)) by Gather(Shape(X), perm) so the expensive Transpose on the full data tensor is avoided.

Before:
         +------------------------+
  x ---> | Transpose perm=[2,0,1] | ---> t
         +------------------------+
                    |
                    v
             +---------------------+
             | Shape start=1 end=3 | ---> y
             +---------------------+

After:
         +-------+
  x ---> | Shape | ---> sx
         +-------+
             |
             v
       +--------------+
       | Gather axis0 | <--- indices=[0,1]
       +--------------+
             |
             v
             y

The permutation is a compile-time attribute of the Transpose node, so the requested dimensions are read directly from Shape(X). The optional start / end attributes of the Shape node select the sub-range perm[start:end] used as the Gather indices. The Transpose is preserved when its output is consumed elsewhere.

Public Functions

inline explicit ShapeTransposePattern(int priority = 0)#

Creates the pattern with the given optimization priority.

virtual std::set<std::string> FastOpType() const override#

Returns Shape as the only possible root operator.

virtual core::builder::MatchResult Match(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const NodeProto &candidate) const override#

Finds a Shape consuming the output of a Transpose with a perm.

virtual utils::RepeatedProtoField<NodeProto> Apply(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const std::vector<const NodeProto*> &nodes) const override#

Rewrites the pair into Gather(Shape(X), perm).

class UnsqueezeShapePattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <shape_pattern.h>

Replaces Shape(Unsqueeze(X, axes)) by a Concat of Shape(X) slices interleaved with constant [1] tensors at the inserted axis positions.

Before:
  x, axes=[1]
       |
       v
  +-----------+
  | Unsqueeze | ---> u
  +-----------+
       |
       v
  +-------+
  | Shape | ---> y
  +-------+

After:
         +---------------------+
  x ---> | Shape start=0 end=1 | ---> s0
         +---------------------+

         +---------------------+
  x ---> | Shape start=1 end=3 | ---> s1
         +---------------------+

  s0, [1], s1
       |
       v
  +--------+
  | Concat | ---> y
  +--------+

Shape(Unsqueeze(X, axes)) equals Shape(X) with 1 entries inserted at the axes positions, so the (potentially large) Unsqueeze on the data tensor is avoided entirely while the shape vector stays identical. The axes input must be a one-dimensional constant and the rank of X must be known. The optional start / end attributes of the Shape node are honoured. The Unsqueeze is preserved when its output is consumed elsewhere.

Public Functions

inline explicit UnsqueezeShapePattern(int priority = 0)#

Creates the pattern with the given optimization priority.

virtual std::set<std::string> FastOpType() const override#

Returns Unsqueeze as the only possible root operator.

virtual core::builder::MatchResult Match(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const NodeProto &candidate) const override#

Finds an Unsqueeze whose output feeds a Shape node.

virtual utils::RepeatedProtoField<NodeProto> Apply(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const std::vector<const NodeProto*> &nodes) const override#

Rewrites the pair into a Concat of ranged Shape slices and [1]s.

namespace onnx_patterns
class SliceSlicePattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <slice_pattern.h>

Merges two consecutive Slice nodes acting on disjoint axes into a single Slice whose starts / ends / axes (and steps when present) are the concatenation of the two operand vectors.

The intermediate result must be consumed by the second Slice alone and both nodes must provide a constant axes input; a missing steps input on either side is materialised as a vector of ones.

Before:
  x, s0, e0, a0, st0
           |
           v
      +-------+
      | Slice | ---> t
      +-------+
                               |
                               v
                         +-------+
                         | Slice | <--- s1, e1, a1, st1
                         +-------+
                               |
                               v
                               y

After:
              +--------+
  s0, s1 ---> | Concat | ---> s
              +--------+
              +--------+
  e0, e1 ---> | Concat | ---> e
              +--------+
              +--------+
  a0, a1 ---> | Concat | ---> a
              +--------+
              +--------+
  st0,st1 --> | Concat | ---> st
              +--------+

  x, s, e, a, st
         |
         v
    +-------+
    | Slice | ---> y
    +-------+

Public Functions

Creates the pattern with the given optimization priority.

Returns Slice as the only possible root operator.

virtual core::builder::MatchResult Match(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const NodeProto &candidate) const override#

Finds a Slice fed by another Slice operating on disjoint axes.

virtual utils::RepeatedProtoField<NodeProto> Apply(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const std::vector<const NodeProto*> &nodes) const override#

Fuses the two slices into a single Slice with concatenated inputs.

class GathersSplitPattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <split_pattern.h>

Merges several sibling Gather nodes reading consecutive constant indices 0, 1, ..., n-1 on the same axis of a common input into a single Split (followed by Squeeze nodes when the indices are scalars).

The axis dimension of the shared input must be statically equal to the number of gathers, so the Split reproduces every original slice.

Before:
                  +--------------+
  x, index=0 ---> | Gather axis1 | ---> y0
                  +--------------+
                  +--------------+
  x, index=1 ---> | Gather axis1 | ---> y1
                  +--------------+
                  +--------------+
  x, index=2 ---> | Gather axis1 | ---> y2
                  +--------------+

After:
         +-------+
  x ---> | Split | ---> t0, t1, t2
         +-------+

                    +---------+
  t0, axes=[1] ---> | Squeeze | ---> y0
                    +---------+
                    +---------+
  t1, axes=[1] ---> | Squeeze | ---> y1
                    +---------+
                    +---------+
  t2, axes=[1] ---> | Squeeze | ---> y2
                    +---------+

After (single-element vector indices):
         +-------+
  x ---> | Split | ---> y0, y1, y2
         +-------+

Single-element vector indices [i] retain the axis, so the Split writes yi directly without Squeeze nodes.

Public Functions

inline explicit GathersSplitPattern(int priority = 0)#

Creates the pattern with the given optimization priority.

virtual std::set<std::string> FastOpType() const override#

Returns Gather as the only possible root operator.

virtual core::builder::MatchResult Match(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const NodeProto &candidate) const override#

Finds sibling Gather nodes covering an axis with constant indices.

virtual utils::RepeatedProtoField<NodeProto> Apply(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const std::vector<const NodeProto*> &nodes) const override#

Replaces the sibling Gather nodes with a Split (plus Squeeze).

class SlicesSplitPattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <split_pattern.h>

Merges several sibling Slice nodes that partition a common input along a single axis into contiguous, non-overlapping ranges into one Split.

Each slice must use a unit step, share the same axis, start where the previous one ends, begin at zero and end at the axis dimension (or the INT64_MAX sentinel used to denote “until the end”).

Before:
                              +-------+
  x, [0], [2], [0] ---------> | Slice | ---> y0
                              +-------+
                              +-------+
  x, [2], [5], [0] ---------> | Slice | ---> y1
                              +-------+
                              +-------+
  x, [5], [INT64_MAX], [0] -> | Slice | ---> y2
                              +-------+

After:
  x, splits=[2,3,1] ---> +-------+ ---> y0
                         | Split | ---> y1
                         +-------+ ---> y2

Public Functions

inline explicit SlicesSplitPattern(int priority = 0)#

Creates the pattern with the given optimization priority.

virtual std::set<std::string> FastOpType() const override#

Returns Slice as the only possible root operator.

virtual core::builder::MatchResult Match(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const NodeProto &candidate) const override#

Finds sibling Slice nodes partitioning an axis into contiguous ranges.

virtual utils::RepeatedProtoField<NodeProto> Apply(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const std::vector<const NodeProto*> &nodes) const override#

Replaces the sibling Slice nodes with a single Split.

class SplitConcatPattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <split_pattern.h>

Replaces a Split immediately followed by a Concat that re-joins all of its outputs, in order and on the same axis, with a single Identity.

Before:
         +-------+
  x ---> | Split | ---> s0, s1
         +-------+

             +--------+
  s0, s1 --> | Concat | ---> y
             +--------+

After:
         +----------+
  x ---> | Identity | ---> y
         +----------+

The rewrite only fires when every Split output feeds the same Concat node, the concatenated inputs are exactly the split outputs in order, and the two axes match (after normalising negative axes against the input rank).

Public Functions

Creates the pattern with the given optimization priority.

Returns Split as the only possible root operator.

virtual core::builder::MatchResult Match(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const NodeProto &candidate) const override#

Finds a Split whose outputs are re-joined by a single Concat.

virtual utils::RepeatedProtoField<NodeProto> Apply(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const std::vector<const NodeProto*> &nodes) const override#

Replaces the matched Split/Concat pair with an Identity.

namespace onnx_patterns
class ExpandBroadcastPattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <expand_pattern.h>

Drops an Expand feeding an element-wise binary operator.

Before:
            +--------+
  x, S ---> | Expand | ---> e
            +--------+

           +--------+
  e, z --> | Binary | ---> y
           +--------+

After:
           +--------+
  x, z --> | Binary | ---> y
           +--------+

S is constant, x and z have the same rank, and every aligned dimension is equal or one. The unshared Expand is removed because Op can broadcast x directly; operand order is preserved.

Public Functions

Creates the pattern with the given optimization priority.

Returns Expand as the only possible root operator.

Finds an Expand consumed by a single broadcasting binary operator.

virtual utils::RepeatedProtoField<NodeProto> Apply(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const std::vector<const NodeProto*> &nodes) const override#

Rebuilds the binary operator on the pre-expanded input.

class ExpandPattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <expand_pattern.h>

Removes an Expand that does not change the shape of its input.

Before:
                            +--------+
  x, shape=[D0,...,Dn] ---> | Expand | ---> y
                            +--------+

After:
                           +----------+
  x ---------------------> | Identity | ---> y
                           +----------+

The rewrite replaces Expand(x, shape) with Identity(x) when the shape of x is fully known and equals the constant shape fed to Expand.

Returns Expand as the only possible root operator.

Finds an Expand whose constant target shape equals its input shape.

virtual utils::RepeatedProtoField<NodeProto> Apply(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const std::vector<const NodeProto*> &nodes) const override#

Replaces the redundant Expand with Identity.

class ExpandSwapPattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <expand_pattern.h>

Moves an Expand past a following unary-like operator.

Before:
            +--------+
  x, S ---> | Expand | ---> e
            +--------+
                 |
                 v
            +----------+
            | UnaryOp  | <--- optional inputs
            +----------+
                 |
                 v
                 y

After:
         +----------+
  x ---> | UnaryOp  | <--- optional inputs
         +----------+
              |
              v
         +--------+
         | Expand | <--- S
         +--------+
              |
              v
              y

The Expand output must be unshared and Op must preserve the shape of its first input. Attributes and any additional inputs of Op are retained, so the operator runs on the smaller tensor.

Creates the pattern with the given optimization priority.

Returns Expand as the only possible root operator.

Finds an Expand consumed by a single unary-like operator.

virtual utils::RepeatedProtoField<NodeProto> Apply(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const std::vector<const NodeProto*> &nodes) const override#

Emits the unary operator first and re-expands its output.

class ExpandUnsqueezeExpandPattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <expand_pattern.h>

Fuses Expand, Unsqueeze and Expand into Unsqueeze then Expand.

Before:
                +--------+
  x, [2,3] ---> | Expand | ---> e1
                +--------+
                    |
                    v
              +-----------+
              | Unsqueeze | <--- axes=[1]
              +-----------+
                    |
                    v
                +--------+
                | Expand | <--- [1,4,3]
                +--------+
                    |
                    v
                    y

After:
                   +-----------+
  x, axes=[1] ---> | Unsqueeze | ---> u2
                   +-----------+
                         |
                         v
                    +--------+
                    | Expand | <--- [2,4,3]
                    +--------+
                         |
                         v
                         y

Both targets and the axes are constant (opset 13 or later), intermediate outputs are unshared, and the ranks agree. The new target is max(insert_ones(first_target, axes), second_target) element by element.

Public Functions

Creates the pattern with the given optimization priority.

Returns Expand as the only possible root operator.

Finds Expand then Unsqueeze then Expand with constant shapes.

virtual utils::RepeatedProtoField<NodeProto> Apply(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const std::vector<const NodeProto*> &nodes) const override#

Emits Unsqueeze on the original tensor and a single trailing Expand.

class ShapeBasedConcatExpandPattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <expand_pattern.h>

Simplifies a dynamic Concat used as an Expand target shape.

Before:
                        +--------+
  p0,...,pk,...,pn ---> | Concat | ---> s
                        +--------+
                            |
                            v
                       +--------+
                       | Expand | <--- x
                       +--------+
                            |
                            v
                            y

After:
                        +--------+
  [1],...,pk,...,[1] -> | Concat | ---> s2
                        +--------+
                            |
                            v
                       +--------+
                       | Expand | <--- x
                       +--------+
                            |
                            v
                            y

Every pi is a one-element vector. The known input and output shapes have equal rank and differ only at dimension k; pk is retained while all unchanged dimensions become 1 so broadcasting preserves them.

Creates the pattern with the given optimization priority.

Returns Expand as the only possible root operator.

Finds an Expand whose dynamic Concat target changes one dimension.

Rebuilds the target shape with [1] for every unchanged dimension.

class ShapeBasedExpandBroadcastMatMulPattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <expand_pattern.h>

Removes dynamic Expand nodes before MatMul.

Before:
             +--------+
  a, sa ---> | Expand | ---> ea
             +--------+

             +--------+
  b, sb ---> | Expand | ---> eb
             +--------+

             +--------+
  ea, eb --> | MatMul | ---> y
             +--------+

After:
           +--------+
  a, b --> | MatMul | ---> y
           +--------+

Either input may already be unexpanded.

Either input may already be unexpanded. Only the leading batch dimensions must broadcast to the output batch shape; the trailing two dimensions retain standard MatMul semantics. Shared Expand nodes remain for other uses.

class ShapeBasedExpandBroadcastPattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <expand_pattern.h>

Removes dynamic Expand nodes before a broadcasting binary operator.

Before:
             +--------+
  a, sa ---> | Expand | ---> ea
             +--------+

             +--------+
  b, sb ---> | Expand | ---> eb
             +--------+

             +--------+
  ea, eb --> | Binary | ---> y
             +--------+

After:
           +--------+
  a, b --> | Binary | ---> y
           +--------+

Either input may already be unexpanded.

The input, pre-expansion, and output symbolic shapes must prove that broadcasting a and b produces the shape of y. Either input may already be unexpanded. Shared Expand nodes are preserved for other consumers, but the rebuilt binary operator bypasses them.

Public Functions

inline explicit ShapeBasedExpandBroadcastPattern(int priority = 0)#

Creates the pattern with the given optimization priority.

virtual std::set<std::string> FastOpType() const override#

Returns broadcasting binary operators as possible roots.

virtual core::builder::MatchResult Match(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const NodeProto &candidate) const override#

Finds a binary operator whose input Expand nodes are unnecessary.

virtual utils::RepeatedProtoField<NodeProto> Apply(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const std::vector<const NodeProto*> &nodes) const override#

Rebuilds the binary operator on the pre-expanded inputs.

class ShapeBasedExpandCastWhereSwapPattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <expand_pattern.h>

Moves an Expand after Cast and Where.

Before:
            +--------+                  +------+
  x, S ---> | Expand | ---> e ---+----> | Cast | ---> condition
            +--------+           |      +------+
                                 |
                                 +--------------------+
                                                      |
                                                      v
                                                   +-------+
  z ---------------------------------------------> | Where | ---> y
                                                   +-------+

After:
         +------+
  x ---> | Cast | ---> condition
         +------+
             |
             +--------------------------+
                                        |
                                        v
                                    +-------+
  z ------------------------------> | Where | ---> w
                                    +-------+
                                        |
                                        v
                                   +--------+
                                   | Expand | <--- S
                                   +--------+
                                        |
                                        v
                                        y

The expanded value may occupy either Where branch.

The expanded value may instead be the false branch. Cast(e) must be the unshared condition, and symbolic shapes must prove that the smaller Where broadcasts to the original output shape.

Public Functions

Creates the pattern with the given optimization priority.

Returns Where as the only possible root operator.

Finds an Expand/Cast/Where chain that can run before expansion.

virtual utils::RepeatedProtoField<NodeProto> Apply(core::builder::GraphGraph &graph, const std::vector<const NodeProto*> &nodes) const override#

Emits Cast and Where on the pre-expanded input, then expands the result.

class ShapeBasedExpandSwapPattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <expand_pattern.h>

Moves input Expand nodes after a broadcasting binary operator.

Before:
            +--------+
  a, S ---> | Expand | ---> ea
            +--------+

            +--------+
  b, S ---> | Expand | ---> eb
            +--------+

             +--------+
  ea, eb --> | Binary | ---> y
             +--------+

After:
            +--------+
  a, b ---> | Binary | ---> t
            +--------+

           +--------+
  t, S --> | Expand | ---> y
           +--------+

Either input may already be unexpanded.

One input may already be unexpanded. Symbolic shapes must prove that the smaller inputs broadcast safely and that the trailing Expand restores the original output shape. Shared input Expand nodes remain for other consumers.

class ShapeBasedStaticExpandPattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <expand_pattern.h>

Replaces a dynamic Expand target with an equivalent constant target.

Before:
                              +--------+
  x, dynamic shape graph ---> | Expand | ---> y
                              +--------+

After:
                              +--------+
  x, constant [1,M,1] ------> | Expand | ---> y
                              +--------+

Dimensions that are unchanged become 1; changed dimensions must be statically known in both input and output and become their output size. The Expand remains, but its dynamic shape computation is replaced.

class SwapExpandReshapePattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <expand_pattern.h>

Swaps an Expand with a following constant-shape Reshape.

Before:
                    +--------+
  x, S=[D,1,1] ---> | Expand | ---> e
                    +--------+
                        |
                        v
                   +---------+
                   | Reshape | <--- [0,1,-1]
                   +---------+
                        |
                        v
                        y

After:
                   +---------+
  x, [0,1,-1] ---> | Reshape | ---> r
                   +---------+
                        |
                        v
                   +--------+
                   | Expand | <--- S=[D,1,1]
                   +--------+
                        |
                        v
                        y

x must have rank three, the Expand output must be unshared, and its inferred target value must end in [1,1]. This specialized form moves the fixed Reshape before expansion.

class SwapExpandUnsqueezePattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <expand_pattern.h>

Swaps an Expand and a following Unsqueeze.

Before:
                +--------+
  x, [A,B] ---> | Expand | ---> e
                +--------+
                    |
                    v
              +-----------+
              | Unsqueeze | <--- axes=[1]
              +-----------+
                    |
                    v
                    y

After:
                   +-----------+
  x, axes=[1] ---> | Unsqueeze | ---> u
                   +-----------+
                         |
                         v
                    +--------+
                    | Expand | <--- [A,1,B]
                    +--------+
                         |
                         v
                         y

The axes are constant (opset 13 or later), the Expand output is unshared, and its target or output shape is known. The new target inserts a 1 at every normalized axis, letting Unsqueeze run before expansion.

namespace onnx_light

Alias that makes onnx-light headers compatible with code that references ONNX_LIGHT_NAMESPACE (the macro used in the standard onnx package).

Set to ONNX_LIGHT_NAMESPACE so both names resolve to the same namespace.

Symbol-visibility attribute for the public onnx-light C++ API.

Maps the upstream compatibility macro to onnx-light’s explicit proto ABI annotation. This keeps declarations from vendored ONNX headers visible when lib_onnx_proto uses hidden visibility by default.

Namespace alias so that ONNX C++ code (and consumers such as onnxruntime) that refers to the literal onnx namespace — rather than the ONNX_NAMESPACE macro — resolves to the onnx-light namespace. The standard onnx package lives in namespace onnx; onnx-light uses onnx_light (via ONNX_LIGHT_NAMESPACE), so this alias keeps onnx-light a true drop-in. It is only introduced when the onnx-light namespace differs from onnx.

class NotWherePattern : public onnx_light::core::builder::PatternOptimization#
#include <where_pattern.h>

Rewrites Where(Not(c), x, y) into Where(c, y, x).

Before:
         +-----+
  c ---> | Not | ---> condition
         +-----+

                      +-------+
  condition, x, y --> | Where | ---> z
                      +-------+

After:
             +-------+
  c, y, x -> | Where | ---> z
             +-------+

The two branches are swapped. A shared Not is preserved for its other consumers while the replacement Where bypasses it.
